evidence.quote: Should the incoming data continue to show that inflation is moving sustainably toward our 2 percent goal, it will become appropriate to gradually lower the federal funds rate
I will remain cautious in my approach to considering adjustments to the current stance of policy.
The progress in lowering inflation since April is a welcome development, but inflation is still uncomfortably above the Committee's 2 percent goal.
That said, I still see some upside risks to inflation as supply conditions have now largely normalized
it appears that the recent rise in unemployment may be exaggerating the degree of cooling in labor markets.
I still see the need to pay close attention to the price-stability side of our mandate while watching for risks of a material weakening in the labor market.

parsed.rationale: The speaker acknowledges that gradual cuts could become appropriate, but stresses patience, caution, upside inflation risks and doubts about labor-market weakness. On net this is a mildly hawkish lean relative to a pending easing cycle.
